newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast minister not standing for OAU job.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast minister not standing for OAU job.

text.p: Ivory Coast has withdrawn Foreign Minister Amara Essy's candidacy for the top job at the Organisation of African Unity, leaving the way clear for incumbent Salim Ahmed Salim to serve a third term.

An official statement published on Friday said the government had decided to withdraw Essy's candidacy for the secretary-general's post "so that our country may never act as a brake on the forward march of our continent".

It gave no further explanation, but political sources said earlier this week the government felt Essy's chances of election were reduced as his support was essentially from francophone countries, many of which were in arrears to the organisation and would not be allowed to vote.
They said Salim's candidacy benefited from the support of South Africa.

Essy, a long-serving and respected foreign minister, was president of the United Nations General Assembly from 1994 to 1995. He was Kofi Annan's closest rival for the post of U.N. secretary general last year.
Salim, a former Tanzanian foreign minister and diplomat, has headed the 53-member OAU since 1989 and is seeking a third four-year term.
